newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT, telecom firms seek rate hike.
newsitem.headline: PLDT, telecom firms seek rate hike.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and other local operators are seeking to increase monthly basic telephone charges by 100 pesos, a source in the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) said on Thursday.
The industry claims the increase will allow it to cover additional costs due to inflation and the declining subsidy from international calls to local telephone companies, the source said.
At present, local operators charge an average flat monthly rate of 250 pesos regardless of the length of local calls.
The source said the companies had proposed a 350 peso new monthly rate to cover 500 minutes of local calls. Beyond 500 minutes, subscribers will be charged 50 centavos for every additional minute.
Local telephone company officials met NTC officials last Monday to discuss the proposed rate adjustment and plan to file a formal application next month, the source said.
NTC head Simeon Kintanar has said public hearings will have to be conducted on the proposed rates, the source added.
